costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz M260 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M260 engine typically takes 10-14 hours at £75-£95/hr (modern Mercedes specialist) - the tight packaging of the transverse engine bay and 48V components makes extraction moderately labour-intensive.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the health of the 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG), the turbocharger, and the plastic coolant housing assemblies. Because the M260 is a highly complex modern unit, reputable recon specialists will typically test the ISG, replace all brittle plastic coolant components with updated revisions, and perform a full software calibration as standard. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz M260 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) Faults
items.whatHappens: The ISG, which replaces the traditional alternator and starter motor, is prone to internal electrical faults or software glitches. This triggers a "48V Electrical System Fault" warning, leading to a no-start condition, limp mode, or the engine failing to restart after an auto-stop.
items.repairVsReplace: Early ISG units were subject to manufacturer recalls and software updates. If the hardware has failed, the entire ISG unit must be replaced, which is a costly but straightforward bolt-on procedure.

items.title: Coolant Leaks (Electric Water Pump & Thermostat Housing)
items.whatHappens: The M260 utilizes several plastic coolant housing components and an electric auxiliary water pump. Over time, constant heat cycles cause these plastic components to warp or crack, leading to external coolant leaks or internal mixing.
items.repairVsReplace: Mercedes has released updated, more durable revisions of these components. Replacing the faulty housing and pump is a standard repair, but ignoring it can lead to overheating and severe engine damage.

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear
items.whatHappens: While generally robust, some early M260 engines exhibited premature timing chain stretch or guide wear, manifesting as a faint rattling noise on cold starts or camshaft position correlation fault codes.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the timing chain kit and updated guides is a known, albeit labour-intensive, repair. If ignored, it can lead to timing jumps and catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

items.title: Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
items.whatHappens: As a direct injection (CGI) engine, fuel does not wash over the back of the intake valves. Combined with the PCV system routing oil vapours into the intake tract, hard carbon deposits bake onto the valves, restricting airflow.
items.repairVsReplace: This causes rough idling, hesitation, and reduced power. The definitive repair is a professional "walnut blasting" service to clean the intake ports and valves.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2021 M260 engines feature revised ISG hardware, updated coolant component materials, and improved timing chain tensioners, making them significantly more robust and reliable than the initial launch models .

variants.title: M260 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ INTRO: The M260 family shares the same fundamental 2.0L DOHC inline-4 block architecture and 48V mild-hybrid foundation, but turbocharging strategy, ECU mapping, and output vary slightly depending on the specific model application. Identifying your exact sub-code is mandatory. - Fitted to: A-Class W177 (A 200), CLA-Class C118 (CLA 200), GLA-Class H247 (GLA 200), GLB-Class X247 (GLB 200) - Key technical difference: The standard-output variant, relying on a single twin-scroll turbocharger and the 48V ISG for smooth power delivery and efficiency. Calibrated for optimal fuel economy and daily drivability. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; ISG and coolant housing leaks are the primary wear items. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the higher-output .920 variant due to different ECU mapping, turbo calibration, and exhaust configurations. - Fitted to: A-Class W177 (A 220), CLA-Class C118 (CLA 220), GLA-Class H247 (GLA 220), GLB-Class X247 (GLB 220) - Key technical difference: The higher-output variant, featuring a revised turbocharger calibration, slightly more aggressive camshaft profile, and specific AMG-Line or higher-trim engine management to deliver stronger mid-range torque and acceleration. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; the higher continuous thermal loads can slightly accelerate coolant component degradation. - Interchange note: Requires matching ECU calibration and specific wiring harness routing; not a direct drop-in for .910 chassis without modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M260 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: Buying a used M260 engine carries significant financial risk unless it comes with a full, stamped service history and documented proof that the ISG and coolant components have been inspected or replaced under warranty. Given the high cost of modern Mercedes electronics, purchasing a used unit with unknown history is highly discouraged.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M260 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by testing or replacing the 48V ISG, upgrading all plastic coolant components to the latest revised factory parts, and ensuring the timing chain assembly is within strict factory tolerances.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M260 engine rebuild is highly justified for high-mileage A 220 or CLA 220 models where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include precision balancing and the installation of the absolute latest factory-revised components.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M260 engine is installed by specialists equipped with the latest Mercedes diagnostic software to calibrate the 48V system, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M260 is found in modern compact vehicles valued between £15,000 and £35,000+, a full engine replacement is a financially viable necessity to protect the asset's value. However, due to the high cost of the engine and specialized labour, always ensure the replacement cost is weighed against the vehicle's current market valuation .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes M260 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes M260 engine typically costs between £3,500 and £5,500 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £4,500 to £6,800 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £1,500 but carry a high financial risk due to the potential for 48V ISG and coolant component failures. → Compare M260 engine replacement quotes today

items.question: What is the most common failure on the M260 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) faults, plastic coolant housing and electric water pump leaks, and early timing chain stretch. The ISG can trigger no-start conditions or limp mode, while degraded plastic coolant components can lead to overheating if not addressed promptly. → Get quotes for a rebuilt M260 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M260 engine?
items.answer: The M260.910 and .920 variants are fitted to the W177 A-Class (A 200, A 220), the C118 CLA-Class (CLA 200, CLA 220), the H247 GLA-Class (GLA 200, GLA 220), the X247 GLB-Class (GLB 200, GLB 220), and the W247 B-Class (B 200, B 220), serving as the definitive modern transverse inline-4 for these chassis from 2018 onwards. → Check your registration to confirm your exact M260 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M260 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned M260 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by testing or replacing the 48V ISG, upgrading all plastic coolant components to the latest revised factory parts, and verifying the timing chain assembly, whereas a used engine with unknown history risks immediate, costly electrical or cooling system repairs. → Compare reconditioned M260 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between M260.910 and M260.920?
items.answer: The M260.910 is the standard-output variant (163 hp) found in A 200, CLA 200, etc., relying on standard turbo calibration for optimal fuel economy. The M260.920 is the higher-output variant (190 hp) found in A 220, CLA 220, etc., featuring a revised turbocharger calibration and more aggressive engine management for stronger mid-range torque. They share the same core block, but the ECU mapping and turbo hardware differ significantly. → Enter your reg above to identify your exact M260 sub-code ═══════════════════════════════════════
